ops.title: capt-hook logs writes nothing: per-session logging dead fleet-wide since 2026-07-30
ops.description:
`capt-hook logs` has produced nothing for any session in about a month, on **both** fleet hosts. Found 2026-08-29 while running the standing capt-hook verification (cc-notes runbook `68af1c77`).

## Evidence

Primary workstation, `~/.cache/captain-hook/logs/`:

```
total log files:      81
newest mtime:         Jul 30 23:31:44 2026
non-empty:            12   (of 81)
written in last 30d:  2
```

`capt-hook logs --session <id>` for two sessions that had just run — one long interactive, one fresh headless — both returned:

```
No log file at /Users/yasyf/.cache/captain-hook/logs/<id>.log
```

No file is created at all; this is not an empty-file problem, it is a not-written-at-all problem.

`yasyf-forge-studio`, independently verified in the same pass: 9 log files, **every one 0 bytes**, dated Aug 20–27, including files named like deliberate probes (`captest.log`, `e2e.log`, `live.log`). `capt-hook logs --session <id>` returned `No log file` for all three sessions run there during verification.

So: two hosts, same symptom, different file counts — a shared code path rather than local corruption.

## Dispatch itself is healthy — this is observability only, not function

Worth stating plainly so nobody chases a phantom outage. On the same hosts, in the same window:

- `capt-hook heartbeats --session <id>` returns a full ledger. A long session showed 11 event types (`PreToolUse ×2890`, `PostToolUse ×2828`, `SubagentStart ×81`, `SubagentStop ×173`); a fresh headless session showed the correct minimal lifecycle `SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/Stop/SessionEnd ×1`.
- On forge-studio a session prompted to run `grep -rn` had the guard **fire and rewrite it** to `ccx code grep` — enforcement observed live, not inferred.
- Hook discovery enumerates 137 hooks across 12 packs.

Hooks dispatch and enforce correctly. What is gone is the per-session record of *what happened*.

## Why it matters

capt-hook is the framework every Claude Code session in this fleet runs on, and the standing instruction is that it is the thing we absolutely cannot break. Right now `heartbeats` is the **only** dispatch signal — it gives per-event counts but no detail, so when something does go wrong there is no per-session log to read. That is precisely the situation in which the log would be worth having.

It also silently degrades the verification runbook: step "inspect `capt-hook logs`" cannot pass on either host today, and a reader could reasonably mistake `No log file` for a broken session rather than a broken logger.

## Where to start

Whatever writes `~/.cache/captain-hook/logs/<session>.log` stopped on or around **2026-07-30 23:31** on the primary workstation — that timestamp is the sharpest lead available and worth bisecting against captain-hook's release history for that week. The mix on forge-studio of 0-byte files *created* as recently as Aug 27 suggests the file may still be opened while nothing is written to it, which would point at a writer/flush path rather than at path resolution.

ops.text: capt-hook logs --session <id> returns the log for a session that just ran, on both fleet hosts
A newly created session log is non-empty and contains that session's hook dispatch records
Root cause is identified for why writing stopped around 2026-07-30 rather than only restored
